reading.body:
Robin Kelly's AI record is legislative and financial, not infrastructural: three cosponsorships, four recorded votes, and four PAC contributions, with no data here on data centers, power, or compute.

The pattern is a lawmaker working the governance layer of AI. The three cosponsorships are all accountability and civil rights bills, H.R. 1694, H.R. 5511, and H.R. 6356, and the four recorded votes are all Yea. The money arrives from the same industry the bills would regulate: Meta Platforms PAC twice, Amazon PAC, and Google NetPAC, between March 2025 and August 2026. One contribution is recorded as $-,500, which is a data defect, not a figure to interpret.

For AI specifically, this is the part of the stack that decides rules rather than runs workloads. Nothing in these eleven events touches siting, interconnection, or electricity supply, so the record cannot speak to whether this lawmaker has engaged with the grid constraint. It also cannot establish that any contribution influenced any vote. The events are listed in date order only, and the page states that placement is not a causal claim.

What the data does not cover is large. It holds only AI-related items, so it is not a full voting or fundraising record. The three news stories are dated September 2026 and two of them name Mark Kelly rather than Robin Kelly, which the entries flag as duplicates. The bill titles beyond the three named cosponsorships are not given, so the subject matter of H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, and S. 146 is unknown from this data alone.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Robin Kelly: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 11 events, and 3 news stories that name them.
